cultural.vision_reason: This is a finely carved wooden killer-whale headdress with typical Northwest Coast formline painting (black, red, green), consistent with Kwakwaka'wakw ceremonial regalia used in dance; carved dance headdresses of this type are well within the tradition. Though filed as "garment," it is worn ceremonial regalia rather than woven cloth.

physical.title: head-dress
physical.summary: Finely carved headdress in the form of a killer whale. The head is carved from a single piece of wood, with side fins and tail fin hinged to it using vegetable fibre twine. The deeply carved face is painted green around the eyes and round the mouth red, as are the shallower figures depicted on the side fins. Other parts of the headdress are blocked out in black. The side fins are restrained with vegetable fibre chord. The tail fin is in two parts, hinged at the centre, with a slot into which a dorsal fin was formerly housed - the right hand tip has been broken.

cultural.vision_reason: A carved wooden human-face mask with mane of hair, identified as Nuhlmahl from the Kwakiutl (Kwakwaka'wakw) Winter Ceremonies — a well-documented ritual object type of this culture.

physical.title: mask
physical.summary: Wood human face mask for use in the Kwakiutl Winter Ceremonies. This large mask is carved with exceptional skill, the horizontal cross section containing a sharp, almost perpendicular angle so that the mask would fit right round the front of the head. Representing Nuhlmahl, a dirty unkempt creature, the imagery is said [by Bill Holm (University of Washington)] to derive from the wood figure on the prow of an early Euro-American ship on the Northwest Coast, but this idea is yet to be fully published. The head is surrounded by a carved mane of hair, painted a yellow or brown colour, with two exaggerated curvilinear ears that seem to be turning into hair. The domed forehead ends in three round segmented raised balls between the large raised eyebrows. These begin with vertical dashes next to the nose and continue with long downward sloping lines extending almost to the ears. The eyes, deeply set on almost flat planes, are cut with circular holes with copper surrounds. The raised cheeks extend down to raised, black painted whiskers, and a thin deeply carved mouth with downturned corners. The large smoothly carved 'Roman' nose is carved with circular openings for nostrils which are pierced through to the other side of the mask at the back. The face is painted red. The upper 40% of the rim is pegged with bunches of black horsehair. The interior is neatly carved with the the thick rim and nose neatly excavated, and the eyes forming slight domes projecting back towards the face of the wearer. The mask is very badly wormed, and has been broken in half down the axis. Much of the paint surface, over spongy decayed areas, has been replaced, and does not look original. It is possible that there was once a grommet, but there is, in the areas where you would expect the holes to be, much damage and restoration.

physical.title: mask
physical.summary: Mask made of wood, hair (human?), hide, cloth, metal, bone (fish?), string, sinew, sea-lion whisker. Blue base, red lips and nostrils, broad black eyebrows, no ears.
